ranAgainst: commit 31220ff plus `git show ":^src/a.ts"` and `git show ":^"` in the unresolvable-colon-words unit test, and the form `git show :^src/a.ts` in the refused-forms-are-real-leaks describe
reason: Found by the fresh documentation review (round 5): `:^` is pathspec negation in git, a synonym of `:!`. checkGitObjects refused a path part starting with `/`, `!` or `(` and judged `^src/a.ts` as a plain path, so `git show :^src/a.ts` was admitted; git reads it as an exclude pathspec and shows HEAD's patch for every other path. Run: 198 tests, 196 pass, 2 fail (the unit test and the integration leak test; the hook assertion fails first in both).
failingTests: git object reads and output forms (CR-01) > unresolvable colon words: a brace, a leading slash, bang or parenthesis, and an absolute path part deny shell-git-object
refused git forms are real leaks > git show :^src/a.ts: denied shell-git-object, and git does print the sentinel
passingAtBase: all 196 other tests of the two files
semanticAssessment: Both failures are on the planned assertion for the intended reason: the hook allows a form the plan refuses. The tests executed on the sentinel-bearing repository; no failure is a syntax, import or fixture fault. Whether real git prints the sentinel for the form is asserted in the leak test after the hook assertion and is observed in the GREEN run.
